name: AI-Data Driven Question Blueprint
purpose: Define stable semantic metadata for full-corpus Lecture-grounded question generation, maximum supported variety, and persistent semantic de-duplication.
runtimePolicy: GitHub Pages does not call an external AI model. AI analyzes the eligible Lecture corpus during automation/build time and writes structured question blueprints for the shared runtime engine.

lectureCorpusPolicy.scope: For every course, recursively include every file under Lecture or 01_Lectures, including files in nested folders.
lectureCorpusPolicy.onlyExclusion: Exclude only files whose real filename identifies Week 0 or Week 0.x.
lectureCorpusPolicy.weekZeroMatching: Match Week/วีค 0 and 0.x case-insensitively and tolerantly for parentheses, spaces, and separators, while never excluding Week 10, 20, 10.1, or other nonzero weeks.
lectureCorpusPolicy.nameDoesNotExclude: Files named Exercise, In-Class Exercise, การบ้าน, เอกสารเพิ่มเติม, Review, Group, Individual, or any other name remain eligible if they are physically under Lecture/01_Lectures and are not Week 0/0.x.

requiredQuestionMetadata.semanticId: Stable ID for one distinct learning objective, relation, condition, interpretation, application, case, exception, or decision. Rewording, option shuffling, answer ordering, or equivalent framing must keep the same semanticId.
requiredQuestionMetadata.conceptIds: Stable IDs for Lecture-grounded concepts/relations used by the question.
requiredQuestionMetadata.sourceRefs: Eligible Lecture file references that directly support the question, answer, distractors, and explanation. Week 0/0.x references are forbidden.

optionalMetadata.difficultyReason: Why the blueprint belongs to Easy/Medium/Hard at university level.
optionalMetadata.blueprintType: definition | relation | comparison | interpretation | application | case | exception | decision | multi-concept
optionalMetadata.semanticFingerprint: Normalized summary used by AI to detect near-duplicate blueprints.

coverageRules: Read every eligible Lecture file, not a sample subset.
Track coverage by source file so eligible Lecture files with testable content are not silently ignored.
Use the full corpus to maximize distinct Lecture-supported learning objectives and relations.
There is no fixed quota or hard question-bank ceiling.
dedupeRules: Never create a new semanticId only because wording changes.
Never create a new semanticId only because choice order, matching order, distractor order, sentence direction, or serial changes.
Check semantic and near-duplicates across the entire course blueprint set, not only within one mode or level.
Merge or skip blueprints that test the same learning objective/relation/condition/case with equivalent Lecture evidence.
Prefer a new blueprint only when it tests materially different Lecture-supported substance.
Question id/serial/option order must never be used as proof that a question is semantically new.
Native and runtime-generated questions that test the same Lecture relation or learning objective must resolve to the same semantic identity whenever derivable.

endlessPolicy.goal: Endless as far as the eligible full Lecture corpus genuinely supports.
endlessPolicy.method: Maximize distinct semantic blueprints through supported definitions, relations, comparisons, conditions, interpretations, applications, cases, exceptions, decisions, multi-concept links, and evidence-backed combinations.
endlessPolicy.noFakeEndless: Do not recycle, reword, reorder, reshuffle, or invent unsupported facts/cases to simulate new questions.
endlessPolicy.exhaustionBehavior: Stop before semantic repetition when no unseen blueprint remains, then re-check current AI-driven data.

runtimeDedupeRules: Persist used semantic signatures across refreshes, tabs, and browser sessions using persistent browser storage when available; session-only storage is insufficient.
Mark a semantic signature as used as soon as the question is displayed, not only after the user submits an answer.
Track used semantic signatures by course+mode+level and maintain recent concept history by course.

If semanticId is missing in data, derive a conservative content-based semantic fingerprint from normalized prompt, correct answer/relation, and Lecture-grounded structure; do not fall back to q.id as the primary semantic identity.
When no unseen semantic blueprint remains, stop rather than repeating semantic substance.
qualityRules: All facts, answers, distractors, and explanations must be supported by eligible Lecture files.
Week 0 and Week 0.x must never support exam knowledge or question metadata.
Easy, Medium, and Hard must remain university-level.
Wrong-answer explanations must state why the submitted answer is wrong using Lecture evidence.
If the eligible Lecture corpus cannot support another semantically distinct blueprint, do not invent new facts merely to preserve endless flow.
